input: Create a vision board for this year's goals

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which life areas (career, health, relationships, finances, travel, etc.) are included determines how broad or focused the board needs to be and how many sections to plan for.
Whether this is a solo personal board or a shared one (with a partner, family, or team) changes the content, tone, and how decisions about imagery and goals are made.
Whether the board will be displayed physically (bedroom wall, office) or used digitally (desktop wallpaper, app) fundamentally changes the format and materials needed.
Available time and budget affect whether the user buys magazines, prints photos, uses premium design tools, or sticks to free resources.
The specific tool or method (physical collage, Canva, Pinterest board, Notion, etc.) determines the exact steps and materials required to get started.
The visual style (minimalist, vibrant, photo-heavy, word-heavy, aesthetic theme) shapes the design choices and what content to source.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — whether it's something they glance at daily for motivation, share publicly, or use in a structured review process — defines the bar for completion.

gold.taskTitle: Create a vision board for this year's goals
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to build a vision board to visually represent and manifest their goals for the current year.

questions.title: Which life areas should the board cover?
questions.description: Identify whether the vision board spans multiple areas (career, health, relationships, finances, travel, personal growth) or focuses on one specific domain, so the scope and sections can be planned accordingly.

questions.title: Is this board just for you, or shared with others?
questions.description: Determine if this is a solo personal board or a collaborative one made with a partner, family member, or team, as this affects whose goals and imagery are represented.

questions.title: Will the board live physically or digitally?
questions.description: Establish whether the vision board will be a tangible physical collage displayed on a wall or a digital artifact used on a screen, since this fundamentally changes materials and format.

questions.title: What tool or platform do you want to use?
questions.description: Pinpoint the specific method — such as a physical poster board, Canva, Pinterest, Notion, or a dedicated vision board app — to determine the exact steps and resources needed to start.

questions.title: How much time and money can you spend on this?
questions.description: Clarify the budget (for printing, magazines, craft supplies, or premium tools) and the time available (a single session vs. multiple sittings) to tailor the plan to realistic constraints.

questions.title: What visual style or aesthetic are you going for?
questions.description: Understand the preferred look and feel — minimalist and clean, bold and colorful, photo-driven, quote-heavy, or a specific mood or color palette — to guide content sourcing and design decisions.

questions.title: How do you plan to use the board once it is done?
questions.description: Determine the intended role of the finished board — daily motivation glanced at each morning, a structured monthly review tool, something to share on social media, or a private reference — to define what 'done well' really means.
